name: apple-hig
description: Use when designing, implementing, or reviewing interfaces for iOS, iPadOS, macOS, tvOS, visionOS, watchOS, CarPlay, or other Apple system experiences using Apple's Human Interface Guidelines. Routes to current platform, foundation, pattern, component, input, and technology guidance.
license: MIT
metadata:
  author: AyushRajSinghParihar
  source: https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines

# Apple Human Interface Guidelines

Use the relevant Apple guidance to make concrete design decisions. This package
contains a router, 13 topic skills, and original article-level references. It is
independent of Apple. The sources are a dated English HIG snapshot; check the
official source when a task depends on a newer release or a disputed detail.

## Route the task

1. Identify the target platform, device context, and user task from the request or
   project. Ask for the platform only when it materially affects the answer and
   cannot be inferred. Preserve the user's framework and product requirements.
2. Select the relevant family below. Read that family's `SKILL.md`, then only the
   article references needed for the task. Nested skills are explicitly read by
   file path; automatic nested discovery is not required.
3. For an exact component, technology, or unfamiliar term, search the
   [complete topic index](references/topic-index.md). It links directly to local
   article references. Do not load the full corpus for a narrow question.
   For a screenshot-specific or animated example, also consult its
   [original visual explanation](references/media/index.md) when available.
4. Apply shared guidance and the target platform's documented differences. A
   missing platform subsection means no additional rule is stated; it does not
   prove support, nonapplicability, or identical behavior across platforms.
5. Compose families when the task crosses them: a component can also require
   accessibility, typography, localization, input, or system-experience guidance.
   Use [platform and task routes](references/platforms-and-tasks.md) when useful.

All paths are relative to **this installed package**, not the shell's current
directory. No Python, network, sibling skill installation, or authoring cache is
required to read the guidance.

| Task | Read this topic skill |
|---|---|
| Platform conventions, design principles, games, device adaptation | [Getting started](subskills/apple-hig-getting-started/SKILL.md) |
| Accessibility, typography, color, materials, layout, localization, privacy | [Foundations](subskills/apple-hig-foundations/SKILL.md) |
| Onboarding, loading, search, sharing, accounts, feedback, media, settings | [Patterns](subskills/apple-hig-patterns/SKILL.md) |
| Charts, images, text views, embedded web content | [Content](subskills/apple-hig-content/SKILL.md) |
| Lists, collections, split views, tab views, disclosure and grouping | [Layout and organization](subskills/apple-hig-layout-and-organization/SKILL.md) |
| Buttons, menus, toolbars, menu bar, ornaments and actions | [Menus and actions](subskills/apple-hig-menus-and-actions/SKILL.md) |
| Sidebars, tab bars, search fields, tokens and path controls | [Navigation and search](subskills/apple-hig-navigation-and-search/SKILL.md) |
| Alerts, sheets, popovers, panels, scrolling and windows | [Presentation](subskills/apple-hig-presentation/SKILL.md) |
| Text fields, pickers, sliders, toggles, selection controls | [Selection and input](subskills/apple-hig-selection-and-input/SKILL.md) |
| Progress, activity, gauges and ratings | [Status](subskills/apple-hig-status/SKILL.md) |
| Widgets, Live Activities, notifications, Siri snippets and system surfaces | [System experiences](subskills/apple-hig-system-experiences/SKILL.md) |
| Touch, keyboard, pointer, focus, eyes, gestures, controllers and sensors | [Inputs](subskills/apple-hig-inputs/SKILL.md) |
| Apple Pay, purchases, Siri, VoiceOver, AI, CarPlay and integrations | [Technologies](subskills/apple-hig-technologies/SKILL.md) |

## Apply the guidance

- **Design:** connect each important choice to the user's task and target
  platform. Include necessary interaction states, adaptation, and accessibility.
- **Implement:** prefer the project's native system components when they supply
  the needed behavior. HIG explains experience requirements; verify API names,
  availability, and code against the appropriate SDK documentation.
- **Review:** describe the observed problem, its effect, the relevant HIG rule,
  and a concrete correction. Separate source-backed findings from your own
  suggested improvements. Do not invent violations without inspecting evidence.

Include official article/section links for material recommendations. Preserve
qualifications such as “consider,” “prefer,” and “avoid”; do not turn design
advice into invented universal requirements. Retain units and platform scope for
numerical specifications. If source passages conflict, describe the conflict
and the conservative application rather than silently changing the source.

## Source boundaries

This is comprehensive local guidance, not a verbatim Apple manual or an SDK API
reference. Original media explanations are supplementary to article references;
the source page remains useful for visual demonstrations. Source snapshots and
review status live in the repository's coverage report, outside ordinary skill
loading. Do not infer that a source has been independently reviewed just because
its local file exists.

Historical `navigation-bars` links now resolve to current Toolbars guidance;
`in-app-purchase` resolves to Apple In-App Purchase. The old Touch Bar and Messages
for Business HIG pages were unavailable at this snapshot. Do not fabricate their
current rules. Translations, archived pages, and complete linked SDK/WWDC libraries
are outside the source boundary.

# Apple HIG: system experiences

Choose the system surface by duration and intent: a widget for periodic glanceable content, Live Activity for a bounded evolving task, notification for a timely event, control/shortcut for a direct action, and complication for watch-face information. Define privacy, deep links, state freshness, and fallback behavior. Consult exact family dimensions and platform contexts; shared frameworks do not imply identical support or interaction.

Read the relevant article below before prescribing behavior. Its platform sections qualify shared guidance; absence of a platform-specific section does not imply unsupported behavior. Articles are original guidance tied to the dated official source.

- [App Shortcuts](references/app-shortcuts.md)
- [Complications](references/complications.md)
- [Controls](references/controls.md)
- [Live Activities](references/live-activities.md)
- [Notifications](references/notifications.md)
- [Snippets](references/snippets.md)
- [Status bars](references/status-bars.md)
- [Top Shelf](references/top-shelf.md)
- [Watch faces](references/watch-faces.md)
- [Widgets](references/widgets.md)

# Live Activities Source: [Apple Human Interface Guidelines](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/live-activities) Snapshot: 2026-10-25. Original implementation guidance derived from the source. ## Contents - [Anatomy](#Anatomy) - [Best practices](#Best-practices) - [Presentation](#Presentation) - [CarPlay](#CarPlay) - [Platform considerations](#Platform-considerations) - [Specifications](#Specifications) Live Activities track a bounded task or event through frequent updates over a few hours. They begin on iPhone or iPad and can appear on the Lock/Home Screen, Dynamic Island and StandBy, paired Mac menu bar, Apple Watch Smart Stack, and CarPlay Dashboard. ## Anatomy Support compact, minimal, expanded, and Lock Screen presentations. The system composes these for available space and devices. ### Compact A single Dynamic Island activity uses separate leading/trailing elements around the TrueDepth camera. ### Minimal Multiple activities use compact circular/oval treatments, up to three where supported: one attached and others detached. Tap opens the app; hold expands. ### Expanded Holding compact/minimal content reveals a larger presentation. ### Lock Screen A bottom banner uses a layout related to expanded. On devices without Dynamic Island, essential update alerts can briefly overlay this banner on Home or another app. ### StandBy Minimal content expands on tap to a Lock Screen layout scaled 2×. A custom background extends across the screen. ## Best practices Use tasks with clear starts and ends, ideally no more than 8 hours. Show only immediately useful information, with details in the app. Exclude ads and promotions. Avoid exposed sensitive content; summarize or redact and offer app access/configuration. Match app identity across appearances; a logo mark can appear without a container, but do not use the full app icon. Do not draw attention to Dynamic Island from inside the app. Use legible large text, generally medium weight or stronger. ### Creating Live Activity layouts Adapt to actual screens and scale factors. Keep layout only as large as content needs. For limited-width Dynamic Island contexts, fit compact/minimal content within a 28-pt circle with abbreviations or graphics; use leading-only when a meaningful trailing version cannot fit. Favor familiar templates, even concentric margins, and container-relative corner radii. Inset groups or use a thick dividing line instead of extending content to edges. A blurred drawing-tool preview can help align angular content within rounded corners. Adjust Lock Screen/expanded height as available information grows or shrinks. ### Choosing colors Only Lock Screen permits custom background colors; compact, minimal, and expanded backgrounds are system-controlled. Dynamic Island is opaque black, so meaningful bold foreground color can express identity. Match its dark-background keyline to related content. Check custom Lock Screen contrast in both appearances and reduced-luminance Always On. ### Adding transitions and animating content updates Animations can last at most 2 seconds and are not played in reduced-luminance Always On. Use numeric changes, fades, scale, or movement to explain updates. Preserve existing elements as layout grows rather than removing/readding everything. Avoid transition collisions; animate a moved item and fade other list elements when needed. ### Offering interactivity Deep-link to the relevant task. Favor one essential button or toggle for a direct action, pause/resume, or response to meaningful progress, preserving space for status and reducing accidental activation. ### Starting, updating, and ending a Live Activity Begin at expected moments, including automatic starts for followed events, with an easy opt-out in the corresponding app view. Offer an App Shortcut when useful. Update only for changed content. Alert only for crucial updates and avoid a parallel push for the same information. Prefer one dynamically changing activity for related simultaneous events. End immediately when the task ends: Dynamic Island/CarPlay remove it, while Lock Screen, Mac, and watch can retain it for up to 4 hours. Choose a shorter useful summary lifetime, commonly 15–30 minutes, proportional to the activity. ## Presentation Design the iPhone presentations first, then tailor layouts for StandBy, watch, and driving while supporting every destination. ### Compact presentation Show essential changing data. Make both halves read as one through coherent color/type and balanced widths. Fit snugly against the camera without extra inner padding or unnecessary status-bar obstruction; shorten units or precision as needed. Both halves should deep-link to the same relevant app screen. ### Minimal presentation Preserve recognition while conveying current information instead of only a static logo. ### Expanded presentation Expand predictably from the smaller layout, retaining relative positions and fitting content close to the camera rather than leaving unused gaps. ### Lock Screen presentation Create a distinct task layout rather than copying notification structure. Use restrained tint/background customization to fit personalized wallpapers. Verify contrast in both appearances and Always On, including the system-generated dismiss-button color; override its foreground if needed. Standard margins are 14 pt, with tighter spacing only when content grouping needs it. ### StandBy presentation Supply assets and, where useful, a custom layout for the larger scale. The default background blends with the bezel and surroundings and permits slightly more content scale. Preserve margins so expansion does not crop graphics, and test the red-tinted Night Mode. ## CarPlay The default combines compact halves. A supplemental small family can support larger type and more information. Its custom layout is also used on watch, but CarPlay disables buttons and toggles; driving-oriented activities should prioritize timely content over those controls. ## Platform considerations No additional iOS or iPadOS rules are specified. Live Activities are unsupported in tvOS and visionOS. ### macOS Paired Mac menu-bar presentations use compact/minimal/expanded styles. Activation opens the app through iPhone Mirroring. ### watchOS The activity appears atop the paired watch's Smart Stack, combining compact halves by default. Tap opens a watch app when available; otherwise it opens a full-screen view with a paired-iPhone launch button. A custom layout can improve essential progress, changes, and controls, but consider its shared use in CarPlay where interaction is disabled. ## Specifications These source dimensions are design guidance in points; system scaling and context can change final appearance. ### CarPlay dimensions Test all three activity sizes and listed Smart Display Zoom simulator configurations. |Live Activity size (pt)| |-----------------------| |240x78 | |240x100 | |170x78 | |Configuration|Resolution (pt)| |-------------|---------------| |Widescreen |1920x720 | |Portrait |900x1200 | |Standard |800x480 | ### iOS dimensions |Screen dimensions (portrait)|Compact (leading and trailing)|Minimal (width given as a range)|Expanded (height given as a range)|Lock Screen (height given as a range)|Limited width| |----------------------------|------------------------------|--------------------------------|----------------------------------|-------------------------------------|-------------| |430x932 |62.33x36.67 |36.67–45x36.67 |408x84–160 |408x84–160 |28x28 | |393x852 |52.33x36.67 |36.67–45x36.67 |371x84–160 |371x84–160 |28x28 | ### iPadOS dimensions |Screen dimensions (portrait)|Lock Screen (height given as a range)| |----------------------------|-------------------------------------| |1366x1024 |500x84–160 | |1194x834 |425x84–160 | |1012x834 |425x84–160 | |1080x810 |425x84–160 | |1024x768 |425x84–160 | ### macOS dimensions Use the iOS dimensions above. ### watchOS dimensions Smart Stack activities use the same dimensions as watch widgets. |Apple Watch size |Size of a Live Activity in the Smart Stack (pt)| |-----------------|-----------------------------------------------| |40mm |152x69.5 | |41mm |165x72.5 | |42mm |176x72.5 | |44mm |173x76.5 | |45mm |184x80.5 | |46mm |194x80.5 | |49mm (Ultra 3, 4)|198x81.5 | |49mm (Ultra 1, 2)|191x81.5 | ## Resources Official implementation links and revision metadata follow. #### Developer documentation — WidgetKit #### Videos ## Change log Revision dates recorded by Apple: October 13, 2026, December 16, 2025, June 10, 2024, October 24, 2023, June 5, 2023, November 3, 2022, September 23, 2022.

item.text: The proposal has five verified issues: promotional starts, exposed address data, a misleading freshness label, indefinite completion display, and catalog content. The local guidance supports automatic starts at expected moments, so I’ll preserve that option for an active delivery and specify an opt-out.

# Delivery Live Activity audit

Decision: revise before implementation. The supplied iOS proposal conflicts with the local Live Activities guidance in five concrete ways. Rankings below are reviewer judgments about user impact, not Apple severity ratings.

## Evidence and route

Inspected [interface.md](interface.md), which contains a textual proposal, not a rendered interface. Read the installed [root procedure](.agents/skills/apple-hig/SKILL.md), then its selected [System experiences family procedure](.agents/skills/apple-hig/subskills/apple-hig-system-experiences/SKILL.md), searched the exact component in the [topic index](.agents/skills/apple-hig/references/topic-index.md), and read the routed [Live Activities source guide](.agents/skills/apple-hig/subskills/apple-hig-system-experiences/references/live-activities.md). The family routes directly to this article; it specifies no additional topic procedure. Paths resolve within this installed package.

Official links below identify the source sections represented by that local guide; they were not fetched. The guide identifies its snapshot as 2026-10-25.

## Ranked verified findings and decisions

| Rank | Observed proposal and effect | Source-backed guidance | Correction / decision |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 — High | Shows the customer's full address on Lock Screen, exposing sensitive delivery information to bystanders. | Avoid exposed sensitive content; summarize or redact and offer app access/configuration. [Best practices](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/live-activities#Best-practices) | Remove the street address, unit and other identifying destination details from the activity payload and display. Use “Your delivery.” Open the relevant order in the app for address details, subject to the app's access controls. |
| 2 — High | Labels a 40-minute-old estimate “Now,” presenting old information as current and encouraging misplaced reliance. | Show immediately useful information; the family procedure explicitly requires state freshness and fallback behavior. [Best practices](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/live-activities#Best-practices) | Display “Estimate unavailable” and “Last updated 40 min ago.” Suppress countdowns based on stale estimates. Define a product freshness threshold and apply it consistently; HIG does not supply a numerical threshold here. |
| 3 — High | Starts automatically for promotional offers without an active delivery, occupying a persistent system surface without a bounded task. | Use tasks with clear starts/ends; exclude ads and promotions. Automatic starts may occur at expected moments, with an easy opt-out in the corresponding app view. [Best practices](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/live-activities#Best-practices), [Starting, updating, and ending](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/live-activities#Starting-updating-and-ending-a-Live-Activity) | No activity for an offer. Start only for a real active delivery at an expected tracking moment. Provide an easy per-delivery opt-out in the order view. Automatic start itself is not the violation. |
| 4 — Medium | Displays “Delivered” forever, retaining an obsolete activity after the task ends. | End immediately when the task ends. Lock Screen may retain the ended summary for up to 4 hours; choose a shorter useful lifetime, commonly 15–30 minutes. [Starting, updating, and ending](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/live-activities#Starting-updating-and-ending-a-Live-Activity) | End on confirmed delivery. Request a 20-minute final Lock Screen summary, then removal; earlier system/user dismissal is acceptable. End cancellation similarly with an appropriate brief summary. Twenty minutes is this design's choice, not a universal HIG requirement. |
| 5 — Medium | Includes a complete shopping catalog in expanded content, burying delivery status and turning tracking into browsing. | Show only immediately useful information, keeping details in the app; favor one essential direct action. [Best practices](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/live-activities#Best-practices), [Offering interactivity](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/live-activities#Offering-interactivity) | Remove the catalog from every activity presentation. Expanded content contains delivery stage, trustworthy ETA/freshness and a relevant order deep link. Catalog browsing remains in the app. |

## Corrected behavior specification

Framework-agnostic policy; lifecycle and scheduling adapters must later be verified against the target platform. No Apple API or SDK is assumed.

"'```text
Policy:
  staleAfter = 5 minutes       // proposed product policy; validate with delivery operations
  finalSummaryLifetime = 20 minutes

on delivery event:
  if event is promotion or there is no real active delivery:
    do not start an activity
    return
  if user opted out for this delivery:
    do not start or restart; end an existing activity if necessary
    return
  start/update only at an expected tracking moment
  use only changed content for updates

render active delivery at currentTime:
  age = currentTime - trustworthy estimate observation time
  if observation time is missing, invalid or in the future:
    etaText = "Estimate unavailable"
    freshnessText = "Update time unavailable"
  else if age > staleAfter or estimate arrival time has passed:
    etaText = "Estimate unavailable"
    freshnessText = localized "Last updated {age} ago"
  else:
    etaText = localized arrival time/range from current estimate
    freshnessText = localized "Updated {age} ago"
  show last confirmed delivery stage; do not infer progress from elapsed time
  never substitute "Now" for an old or absent estimate
  exclude address and catalog data from activity content
  expose a relevant order deep link
  reevaluate freshness when time crosses the threshold, even without a new delivery event

on confirmed delivered/cancelled:
  end the activity immediately
  request final summary until terminalEventTime + finalSummaryLifetime
  omit ETA; show confirmed terminal status and time
  never extend expiry through repeated terminal events
```

The freshness scheduler must not depend solely on receiving another network update. If the eventual platform cannot reliably refresh at the threshold, use a conservative timestamped fallback rather than leave a seemingly current ETA on screen. Network loss alone does not establish cancellation or delivery.

Use a distinct, compact task layout: “Your delivery,” last confirmed stage, then ETA or fallback and update age. Retain those meanings in expanded content. Support compact/minimal presentations with essential changing status and the same order destination. Use standard 14 pt Lock Screen margins, with tighter spacing only for grouping; verify legible text and contrast in both appearances and reduced-luminance Always On. These are implementation acceptance requirements, not observed visual failures. [Anatomy](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/live-activities#Anatomy), [Lock Screen presentation](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/live-activities#Lock-Screen-presentation)

## Worked before / after

At 14:00, delivery D42 is active, its last confirmed stage is “On the way,” and its estimate was observed at 13:20. No newer estimate exists.

| Before: supplied behavior | After: specified behavior |
|---|---|
| Full customer street address | “Your delivery” |
| “Now” based on the 13:20 estimate | “On the way” / “Estimate unavailable” / “Last updated 40 min ago” |
| Complete catalog in expanded content | Same delivery summary, linking to D42 in the app |

At 14:07, a confirmed delivered event arrives. End immediately and show “Delivered at 14:07” as the final summary, requesting removal by 14:27. A repeated delivered event at 14:10 does not extend that deadline. If instead there is only a promotional offer and no delivery, show no Live Activity at all.

## Acceptance checks

These are proposed checks, not executed test results.

- Offer-only input with no active delivery produces no activity. An eligible active delivery can start at the expected moment; opting out ends it and prevents restart for that delivery.
- Inspect every activity payload and presentation: no full address, unit, identifying destination detail, catalog or promotional content is present. Activating its order link resolves to the correct order.
- At 14:00 with an observation timestamp of 13:20, output matches the worked example. Missing/invalid/future timestamps show an honest fallback. A past arrival estimate never becomes “Now.”
- With no network event, advance time beyond the proposed five-minute threshold: stale ETA disappears or a conservative timestamped fallback remains. A new trustworthy update restores the current estimate.
- A confirmed terminal event immediately ends the running activity and requests a final summary expiry 20 minutes from that event. Repeated events do not reset expiry; earlier system/user dismissal is accepted.
- On actual supported devices or suitable rendering tools, verify small screens, longer localized strings and larger text: status and freshness remain legible, with no clipping. Check Lock Screen margins and contrast in light/dark appearances and Always On, including dismiss-button visibility. Verify accessible reading order and meaningful link labeling with accessibility tooling.

## Evidence limits

Only the supplied sentence and installed instructions/source snapshot were audited. All five findings are verified against that textual proposal; their relative severity and the five-minute/20-minute policy values are review decisions. There is no screenshot, implementation, payload, delivery-service contract or rendering evidence. Contrast, typography, touch targets, accessibility behavior, actual deep links, timers, lifecycle execution and system dismissal were not tested. No device, SDK, GUI, simulator, accessibility or automated test execution occurred. This document specifies intended behavior; implementation feasibility and current platform behavior remain to be validated. No web browsing was performed, and current official guidance was not independently verified.
EOF'

| “Now” based on the 13:20 estimate | “On the way” / “Estimate unavailable” / “Last updated 40 min ago” |
| Complete catalog in expanded content | Same delivery summary, linking to D42 in the app |

At 14:07, a confirmed delivered event arrives. End immediately and show “Delivered at 14:07” as the final summary, requesting removal by 14:27. A repeated delivered event at 14:10 does not extend that deadline. If instead there is only a promotional offer and no delivery, show no Live Activity at all.

## Acceptance checks

These are proposed checks, not executed test results.

- Offer-only input with no active delivery produces no activity. An eligible active delivery can start at the expected moment; opting out ends it and prevents restart for that delivery.
- Inspect every activity payload and presentation: no full address, unit, identifying destination detail, catalog or promotional content is present. Activating its order link resolves to the correct order.
- At 14:00 with an observation timestamp of 13:20, output matches the worked example. Missing/invalid/future timestamps show an honest fallback. A past arrival estimate never becomes “Now.”
- With no network event, advance time beyond the proposed five-minute threshold: stale ETA disappears or a conservative timestamped fallback remains. A new trustworthy update restores the current estimate.
- A confirmed terminal event immediately ends the running activity and requests a final summary expiry 20 minutes from that event. Repeated events do not reset expiry; earlier system/user dismissal is accepted.
- On actual supported devices or suitable rendering tools, verify small screens, longer localized strings and larger text: status and freshness remain legible, with no clipping. Check Lock Screen margins and contrast in light/dark appearances and Always On, including dismiss-button visibility. Verify accessible reading order and meaningful link labeling with accessibility tooling.

## Evidence limits

Only the supplied sentence and installed instructions/source snapshot were audited. All five findings are verified against that textual proposal; their relative severity and the five-minute/20-minute policy values are review decisions. There is no screenshot, implementation, payload, delivery-service contract or rendering evidence. Contrast, typography, touch targets, accessibility behavior, actual deep links, timers, lifecycle execution and system dismissal were not tested. No device, SDK, GUI, simulator, accessibility or automated test execution occurred. This document specifies intended behavior; implementation feasibility and current platform behavior remain to be validated. No web browsing was performed, and current official guidance was not independently verified.
